segments.text: I am double vaccinated with AstraZeneca, which has now been withdrawn.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The ministers may understandably wish to defer responsibility for a decision such as withdrawing the vaccines from the population to the regulators, such as the MHRA, or in America it would be the FDA.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Historically, when undertaking the approval of any drug, the regulators themselves ultimately end up relying on the summary results of the drug companies.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: in their sponsored trials, where the raw data is kept commercially confidential.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Furthermore, the MHRA has a huge financial conflict of interest, receiving 86% of its funding from the pharmaceutical industry they are supposed to regulate.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: In effect, Madam Deputy Speaker, we've got the poacher paying the gamekeeper.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: As pointed out in a recent BMJ investigation,
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: into the financial conflicts of interest of the drug regulators, sociologist David Donald Light said of them, it's the opposite of having a trustworthy organisation independently and rigorously assessing medicines.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: They're not rigorous, they're not independent, they're selective and they withhold data.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Doctors and patients must appreciate how deeply and extensively drug regulators can't be trusted so long as they're captured by the industry funding.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Similarly, another investigation revealed that members of the JCVI have huge financial links to the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Running to billions of pounds, the ministers, the media and the public know that the foundation itself is heavily invested in the pharmaceutical industry stock.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Unfortunately, the catastrophic mistake over the approval and the coercion associated with this emergency use authorisation medical intervention is not an anomaly, but in many ways it could have been predicted by structural failures that have allowed this to occur in the first place.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: These shortcomings are rooted in the increasingly unchecked visible and invisible power of multinational corporations, in this case Big Pharma.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: We start by acknowledging that the drug industry has a fiduciary obligation to produce profit for their shareholders.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Madam Deputy Speaker, they have no fiduciary obligation to provide the right medicines for patients.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The real scandal is that those with the responsibility of patients and scientific integrity, namely doctors, academic institutions and medical journals, collude with the industry for financial gain.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Big Pharma exerts its power by capturing the political environment through lobbying, the knowledge environment through funding university research and influencing medical education.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: preference shaping through capture of the media, financing, think tanks, etc.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: etc.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: In other words, the PR machinery of pharma excels in substitute subterfuge, engages in smearing and deplatforming those who call out their manipulations.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
